heading: CHAPTER XX.
title: ARE FORTRESSES, AND MANY OTHER THINGS TO WHICH PRINCES OFTEN RESORT, ADVANTAGEOUS OR HURTFUL?
exclusions: front matter and dedication before THE PRINCE
notes: Chapter 20 tests common princely expedients one by one and refuses to rank them in the abstract. Their value depends on the condition of the state and where the prince's real danger comes from.
The chapter keeps returning to one practical test: does the device make subjects more yours, or does it expose distrust, weakness, or misplaced confidence?
Fortresses receive the chapter's sharpest corrective. They can sometimes help, but they never substitute for not being hated by the people.
